title: Behind the Spike: Medical Device Reporting Trend Review
abstract: An investigation into a sudden increase in FDA reports for PTCA balloon catheters. Using Python, Excel, and original report narratives, I traced the increase to a concentration of older recorded events and identified how registry reporting and incomplete event dates complicated their interpretation.
introduction: In May 2025, FDA reports for the LOX device category increased from 128 to 343. I initially examined the change through monthly counts and event-to-receipt timing, then reviewed the underlying narratives to investigate the unusual pattern.
output: Excel workbook with monthly trends, timing breakdowns, and data-quality checks.
Python workflow for extracting, cleaning, and analyzing 1,922 reports.
Narrative screening of all 343 May reports, with targeted manual validation.
conclusions: Reports listing Boston Scientific accounted for 211 of the net 215-report increase.
229 May reports contained registry references and described year-only event dates.
Date substitution and inconsistencies between structured fields and narratives made exact reporting lags uncertain.
The evidence supports further review of reporting practices, not conclusions about changes in device safety.
ethical_considerations: Unique report keys do not necessarily represent unique clinical incidents.
Possible-duplicate language does not establish actual duplication.
FDA reports alone cannot establish causality or device failure rates.
